$comment:
The grant vocabulary: everything a household can allow or deny per person. Closed, like capabilities.json and permissions.json, so a grant can be rendered, explained and audited rather than being an opaque string.

An entry containing a `<placeholder>` is parameterized: a grant writes it out with a real target (`use:<package>` becomes `use:videos`), the same way a manifest writes `net:api.open-meteo.com` against permissions.json's `net:<host>`. Every other entry is used verbatim. (permissions.json's own comment says 'entries ending in a colon', which describes no entry in either file; the placeholder is the real convention and what the matcher implements.)

Read this next to what it deliberately does NOT contain. There is no action that weakens the safety floor, no 'bypass_safety', no 'disable_filters'. The org's Safety invariants make those non-removable by anyone including the owner, so an action for them would be a lie in a list a family is meant to trust. `chat.unrestricted` and `generate.unrestricted` below are the adult-freedom unlock the standard DOES describe - unfiltered answering for an adult who has acknowledged it - and they still run under the same floor. POLICY (SPEC-CAP-01): every entry carries `policy` (or, for a duplicate id, `policy_ref` naming the file that owns it). `approver` gives, per age band, who must say yes before this runs: none (it runs), self (the person confirms), parent (a household admin must approve; the person's own answer never counts), never (denied). Strictness runs none < self < parent < never. A child's cell is never looser than a teen's, a teen's never looser than an adult's, and `parent` is invalid for an adult. `by_parameter` overrides the cells for one parameter value and is monotonic too. `consequential: true` in a manifest raises a `none` cell to `self` in every band. An id with no policy decides `unknown_default`. `limits` names conditions the gate applies on an allow. `model_callable: false` means no tool, package or host call may hold the id. The adult column records what the hub does today.

actions.description: Use one package: an app, a plugin, a skill. The workhorse: 'Billy cannot use app X' is one deny.
Use any installed package. Pair with a per-package deny for 'everything except X'.
Install a package from the catalog.
Remove an installed package.
Let skills compose into this person's turns at all. Jesse's own example of a global switch a household might want off for one person.
Author a command ('when I say X, do Y').
Reach one connected integration.
Offer the show_images tool when existing turn eligibility permits it.
Answer this adult without content filtering, above the non-removable safety floor. Requires acknowledged_at on the grant; never a default, never inherited.
The same, for generation. Same acknowledgment rule.
Read household-scoped memory. Person-scoped memory is never reachable through a grant; it belongs to its person.
Write household-scoped memory.
Create, edit and remove household profiles. What the owner/admin ladder hard-codes today.
Grant and revoke other people's grants. Held apart from people.manage on purpose: editing a name and handing out authority are different powers, and the second is how a household is taken over.
Change household-wide settings.

Reach the admin area at all. The org rule Jesse set on 2026-09-05 - regular users never see admin settings, even disabled ones - is enforced by rendering nothing without this, rather than by disabling controls.
Pair, rename and remove devices, pods and robots.
Take a backup on demand.
Stage a restore. Replaces every person, memory and conversation in the house, which is why it is its own action and not part of backups.run.
State and correct household-scoped relationships between entities.
Share a file or project outside the person's own space, household-wide or outside the house.
Attach a photo to a chat. Also gated by the household photo-upload setting, which a parent must have turned on for a child.
Send a query to the optional owner-keyed hosted search provider. Never for a child or teen.
A web search whose query names a household member: a family name leaves the house.
Send a notification to another household member. The `admin` parameter value means the recipient is a household admin.
Decide another person's pending approval. Never callable by a model, tool, package or host call: only an authenticated session may hold it.
